sentences.text: But that would not mean that in all cases where an employee disputes his liability, a full-fledged inquiry should be held.

sentences.text: If the discretion given under Regulation 60(1)(b) is misused or is exercised in an arbitrary manner, it is open to the employee to challenge the same before the appropriate forum.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: It is for the disciplinary authority to decide whether regular departmental enquiry as contemplated under Regulation 58 for imposing major penalty should be followed or not.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: This discretion cannot be curtailed by interpretation which is contrary to the language used.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: Further, Regulation 60(2) itself provides that in a case if it is proposed to withhold increments of pay and such withholding of increments is likely to affect adversely the amount of retirement benefits payable to an employee and in such other cases as mentioned therein, the disciplinary authority shall hold inquiry in the manner laid down in Regulation 58 before making any order imposing any such penalty.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: Hence, it is apparent that the High Court erroneously interpreted the Regulation by holding that once the employee denies the charge, it is incumbent upon the authority to conduct inquiry contemplated for imposing major penalty.

sentences.text: It also erred in holding that where an employee denies that loss is caused to the Corporation either by his negligence or breach of order, such inquiry should be held.

The Court held as under:-
"Position after decision in FCI: Where the Rules give a discretion to the Disciplinary Authority to either hold a summary enquiry or regular enquiry, it is not possible to say that the Disciplinary Authority should direct only a regular enquiry, when an employee denies the charge or requests for an inquiry.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text:
Even in such cases, the Disciplinary Authority has the discretion to decide, for reasons to be recorded,
whether a regular enquiry should be held or not.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: If he decides not to hold a regular enquiry and proceeds to decide the matter summarily, the employee can always challenge the minor punishment imposed, on the ground that the decision not to hold a regular enquiry was an arbitrary decision.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: In that event, the Court or Tribunal will in exercise of power of judicial review, examine whether the decision of the Disciplinary Authority not to hold an enquiry was arbitrary.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: If the Court/Tribunal holds that the decision was arbitrary, then such decision not to hold an enquiry and the consequential imposition of punishment will be quashed.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: If the Court/Tribunal holds that the decision was not arbitrary, then the imposition of minor penalty will stand.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

sentences.text:
It is also possible to read the decisions in Bharadwaj and FCI harmoniously, if Bharadwaj is read as stating a general principle, without reference to any specific rules, that it is incumbent upon the Disciplinary Authority to hold a regular enquiry,
even for imposing a minor penalty, if the charge is factual and the charge is denied by the employee.
sentences._hearing_file: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026.json

opennyai_summary.16_July_2025__arguments:
Firstly, he submitted that since the petitioner raised disputed question of facts in his reply,
a detailed departmental enquiry ought to have been conducted by the respondents under Rule 14 of CCA Rules.
Secondly, he submitted that since the petitioner had already retired on 30.09.2020, the punishment order could not have been passed without the approval of the Governor.
The learned counsel for the petitioner also challenged the finding recorded against him in the impugned order on merits.
Counsel for the petitioner placed reliance upon the Apex Court judgment in the case of O.K. Bharadwaj Vs. Union of India &
Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30314626/
He further submitted that the petitioner has not disputed the fact that he was responsible for the safety and security of the forest range and, therefore, since the loss is caused to the Government during the period of his posting, he has been rightly imposed with the punishment of recovery of the amount to the loss caused to the Government.
He further submits that the respondent Divisional Forest Officer was competent to impose punishment upon the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.16_July_2025__ANALYSIS:
However, the judgment passed in the said case was considered and explained by this Court in the case of Roop Singh Bhadouria Vs. State of M.P. & others (W.P.No.7788/2011) .
Considering the aforesaid legal position, if the facts of the present case are seen, the authorities have given detailed reasons while recording the finding against the petitioner.
Since the petitioner was posted in the Forest Range during the aforesaid period, he is rightly been found responsible for illegal excavation.
Thus, it cannot be said that finding recorded by the authorities are perverse or without any justification.
Thus, it is found that the process adopted by the respondents NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:14749 5 WP-19351-2022 in imposing punishment is in consonance with Rule 16 of CCA Rules.

He further submitted that the petitioner has not disputed the fact that he was responsible for the safety and security of the forest range and, therefore, since the loss is caused to the Government during the period of his posting, he has been rightly imposed with the punishment of recovery of the amount of loss caused to the Government.
He further submitted that the respondent Divisional Forest Officer was competent to impose punishment upon the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
In our view, on the basis of the allegation that Food Corporation of India is misusing its power of imposing minor penalties, the Regulation cannot be interpreted contrary to its language.
If the discretion given under Regulation 60(1)(b) is misused or is exercised in an arbitrary manner, it is open to the employee to challenge the same before the appropriate forum.
It is for the disciplinary authority to decide whether regular departmental enquiry as contemplated under Regulation 58 for imposing major penalty should be followed or not.
This discretion cannot be curtailed by interpretation which is contrary to the language used.
Hence, it is apparent that the High Court erroneously interpreted the Regulation by holding that once the employee denies the charge, it is incumbent upon the authority to conduct inquiry contemplated for imposing major penalty.
11. Thus, in view of the discretion conferred on the disciplinary authority under Rule 16, a regular departmental enquiry can be dispensed with depending upon the facts of the case.
However, if the authority decides not to hold a regular enquiry and proceeds to decide the matter summarily, such a decision is open to judicial review by this Court.
12.
It is settled that in exercise of powers of judicial review, this Court can examine the decision making process only.
Thus, findings as recorded in the impugned order are not open to interference in power of judicial review so long as there is some material to support such finding.
So far as the process adopted by the respondents, the same is found to be proper inasmuch as the petitioner was given a show-cause notice to which he submitted his reply.
The reasons have been assigned in the impugned order based upon the material collected during the inspection in presence of the petitioner.
Thus, the requirement of Rule 16 of CCA Rules as also that of principles of natural justice have been satisfied.
The impugned order passed by respondent authority is thus found to be just and proper.
16. On the date, of the impugned order was passed on 25.07.2022, the petitioner had already retired.
18. Thus, by virtue of proviso to Rule 9(2)(a), the authority was required to submit regarding its finding to the Governor and thereafter order could have been passed by the Governor.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Thus, the impugned order, dated 26.07.2022 (Annexure-P/1) is found to have been passed in violation of Rule 9 of the Pension Rules.
Accordingly, upholding the findings recorded in the impugned order, the same is set- aside for want of competence on the part of the respondent/Divisional Forest Officer.
19. The respondents are, however, given liberty to pass a fresh order in accordance with Rule 9 of the Pension Rules.
Let the same be done within a period of 90 days' from the date of submission of the certified copy of this order.
20. With the aforesaid, this writ petition is disposed off.
